items.author: David Senra
items.text:
When @vladtenev arrived in New York from Bulgaria at 5 years old, he said it felt like entering a science fiction world:

“When we landed in America, there was just this huge sea change immediately. The vibe was completely different, and I noticed it as a five-year-old.”

“Every single building would be the tallest building in Bulgaria.”

“It’s like the buildings are competing with each other. There was no competition in Bulgaria.”

“In Bulgaria, you walk around and society's collapsing, all the old ladies are looking down and everyone's moving kind of slowly.”

items.author: Richard D. Bartlett
items.text:
immaculate songwriting irresistibly destroys grumpy feelings. pentecostal big band banger. wait for the drop at 0:55

“I declare and I decree
Any chain that has been holding me
Any evil tongue that whispers in these ears
I said, I rebuke you, you must leave my life
You are not welcome here...

I'm letting it wash over me 
I'm letting it all wash away 
All of it, all of it
It must let go of me today

Cover me with Your feathers, Father
Shelter me with Your wings
I may cry through the night, I may cry through the night
I may cry through the night, but my joy comes in the morning

Joy, joy
I may cry through the night, but my joy comes in the morning
My joy, oh, my joy (joy)
Oh, my joy comes in the morning
My joy comes in the morning”

items.author: Pico Iyer
items.text: Each time a cherished friend dies, a part of us goes with them. Suddenly there are so many corners of oneself we can no longer share or express. And thus we practice death a dozen times before inflicting the same challenge on others.

items.author: Bryan Johnson
items.text:
LSD as a longevity therapy? 

LSD pushes brain gene activity in the opposite direction of aging

In rodents, the effect was stronger than exercise

LSD activated gene networks involved in neuroplasticity and neuronal communication, and reduced amyloid-β damage
